author: framework-coordinator
intent: Preserve the native wrapped raw penalty across the two Base energy social-efficiency branches, including the labs-first copy-clamp-then-double ordering, without changing any other original path.
evidence: The pin test verifies the exact original image SHA, uses match_recovery PeImage/Span, and Capstone-decodes all bytes in the complete 004EB560..004EC3A6 span. It asserts the 004EC212/214 branch to 004EC2A9, labs-first raw IMUL at 004EC21A, copy clamp (`mov eax, esi`) at 004EC22D, raw double at 004EC25B, alternate raw IMUL/double at 004EC2A9/2AC, and the later raw-value test at 004EC2E9.

Concrete labs-first signed-int counterexample: psych=0, labs=134217738, efficiency=-4 yields commerce_delta=134217733 and raw IMUL bits 80000050 (-2147483568). Native labs penalty clamps to zero; doubling raw bits wraps to 160 and economy penalty clamps to 80. The old source instead doubled the clamped labs value, yielding economy penalty zero.

The alternate branch is independently exercised with psych=0, labs=-134217738, efficiency=-4: fallback delta=134217743 selects the economy-first path; raw IMUL wraps to 800000F0 (-2147483408), doubled raw wraps to 480 and clamps the labs penalty to 80, while raw itself clamps the economy penalty to zero.

Use existing base_yield_mul/base_yield_add to model x86 low-word behavior without signed-overflow UB. The host test extracts and executes the complete current base_energy body and actual helpers under available g++/clang++ at -O0 and -O2. It preserves the original uninitialized locals; GCC's corresponding -O2 diagnostic is not promoted to error. A source-body mutant that doubles the clamped labs penalty must fail at the overflow fixture. The pinned-image test uses OPENSMACX_IMAGE or a repository-relative ignored-image fallback and fails, rather than silently skipping, if missing.

No mapping or historical claim is created, removed or changed. Preserve the deliberately uninitialized alien subtotal/ordinal paths and all unrelated behavior. Host controls are not byte-exact recovery, runtime acceptance or full-project acceptance.
